headline: Wholesale inflation hits a record 12.29 percent as AI stocks rattle Wall Street

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Tuesday, the seventeenth of November, and here is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, inflation. Wholesale prices rose 12.29 percent in October, the highest in the current series, and retail inflation has now broken above the Reserve Bank's upper limit of 6 percent. Traders are increasingly betting on a rate hike in December.

Second, Wall Street had a rough night. The Nasdaq fell about two and a half percent as artificial intelligence stocks slid ahead of Nvidia's results tonight, its first since chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down last week. Asian markets are lower this morning, and GIFT Nifty points to a flat, cautious start for us.

And third, a tax story every investor will care about. The chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes says the government is examining proposals to change capital gains tax on equities, with any decision due in the Budget on the first of February.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Now to how markets closed on Monday. The Sensex and the Nifty each gained more than half a percent, led by banks and consumer goods companies. Punjab National Bank, Federal Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Eternal all touched fresh 52-week highs.

Hospitals were the stars of the day. The BSE Hospitals index jumped 3.57 percent, and Max Healthcare rose as much as 7 percent to around 1,008 rupees. On the other side, pharma was the weakest sector, with Laurus Labs, Sai Life Sciences and Divi's falling as much as 10 percent. The broader market slipped too, with the BSE SmallCap 250 down almost 1 percent.

Foreign money keeps coming in. Business Standard reports more than 9 billion dollars of foreign equity inflows so far this month, and the rupee gained 32 paise on Monday, the best performer in Asia, helped by softer crude prices.

The levels to watch: analysts say the Nifty faces resistance at 25,300 to 25,400. A clear move above that could open the way to 25,500 and then 25,650. Support sits at 25,100 to 25,000. Looking further out, Morgan Stanley sees the Sensex at 95,000 by December next year, about 16 percent higher, on better earnings and domestic flows.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
To the primary market. Crystal Crop Protection opens its IPO tomorrow, the eighteenth, and it closes on Friday, the twentieth. The upper end of the price band is 272 rupees, and Livemint reports a grey market premium of about 13 rupees, which points to a modest listing gain of under 5 percent.

The bigger news is from the regulator. The Securities and Exchange Board of India has set up a ten-member panel, headed by National Stock Exchange chief Ashish Chauhan, to review the rules for raising capital. It will look at eligibility, promoter lock-ins, pricing, allotment and disclosures for IPOs, follow-on offers, qualified institutional placements and preferential issues. The aim is to cut duplication and make fundraising simpler.

Sebi is also expected to propose raising the threshold for identifying beneficial owners of foreign portfolio investors from 10 percent to 25 percent, in line with global practice. A consultation paper is due soon.

On deals, SML Mahindra's rights issue of about 1,450 crore rupees opens on the first of December, at 3,506 rupees a share, two shares for every seven held. The money will mainly fund its purchase of Mahindra's truck and bus business. And BSE has received American approval to offer its Bankex futures to investors in the United States.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now the results roundup, and it's a mixed bag.

Among the winners, Belrise Industries saw net profit rise 25 percent to about 166 crore rupees in the September quarter, with revenue up 17 percent, and the shares jumped 13 percent. Kalyan Jewellers reported profit growth of 64 percent and revenue growth of 32 percent, and its stock has now risen 42 percent this month.

In new-age companies, Eternal, the parent of Zomato, grew revenue nearly 78 percent and profit 92 percent. Swiggy's revenue rose 36 percent, but its losses widened from the previous quarter as it spent on quick commerce.

On the other side, Inox Wind's profit fell 42 percent to 69 crore rupees on higher costs, and the stock lost 10 percent. Patanjali Foods slipped 4 percent after a weaker quarter, which Jefferies put down to festive-season timing and pressure on edible oil margins. Kaynes Technology missed estimates, and Jefferies cut its target while keeping its buy rating. And Amber Enterprises gave back 8 percent a day after a 9 percent jump, with Elara Securities and Equirus flagging margin pressure.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
To the economy, where the oil shock is showing up everywhere.

Wholesale inflation climbed to 12.29 percent in October from 11.39 percent in September. Fuel and power did most of the damage, with inflation there jumping to nearly 33 percent. Price pressure is also spreading in the retail basket. Moneycontrol finds mobile phone inflation at 8.65 percent, and 95 of 358 items rising faster than 6 percent. Some analysts now expect the Reserve Bank to lift the repo rate to 6.25 percent.

The trade numbers tell a similar story. October exports hit a record of about 49.5 billion dollars, up 45 percent from a year ago. But imports surged to about 89 billion dollars, so the goods trade deficit widened to nearly 40 billion dollars, a one-year high.

The government has raised the windfall tax on fuel exports. The export levy on diesel goes up to 14 rupees a litre from 11.50, and on aviation fuel to 12.50 rupees. Petrol is unchanged.

There was some good news on jobs. Unemployment eased to 4.9 percent in October, an eight-month low, as more women joined the workforce, especially in rural areas.

And ahead of the Budget, economists told Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to treat the oil shock as a one-time event, stick to the debt-reduction path and keep spending on infrastructure, even with Pay Commission costs coming.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, the artificial intelligence trade is being tested. On Wall Street, the Nasdaq fell 2.5 percent, the S and P 500 lost 1.9 percent and the Dow slipped 1.4 percent, while the fear gauge jumped 25 percent. Chipmakers were hit hardest. Nvidia fell another 4 percent on Monday and is down nearly a quarter this month, after Jensen Huang's exit as chief executive last week. A report says the board is not considering bringing him back. Nvidia reports results after the American close tonight, and Anthropic's Nasdaq listing is due on Thursday.

Adding to the pressure, Washington has tightened curbs on Chinese companies using advanced chips in data centres in Thailand and Malaysia. In Asia this morning, Korea's Kospi is down 2 percent and Japan's Nikkei 1.3 percent.

The dollar has hit its highest level since April last year, wiping out all its losses since the Liberation Day tariffs, as traders bet on American rate hikes. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said gradual hikes would be appropriate.

Oil eased. Brent fell about three and a half percent to near 92 dollars a barrel after the International Energy Agency flagged a supply surplus, though tensions in the Strait of Hormuz remain. Goldman Sachs expects Brent to ease to 78 dollars by December next year. And gold is near a 14-month low, around 3,850 dollars an ounce, with Goldman saying it may take two years to reclaim its record.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, starting with capital gains tax. Central Board of Direct Taxes chairman Ravi Agrawal says the Finance Ministry is studying proposals on long-term capital gains tax and the securities transaction tax. Industry bodies have asked for long-term capital gains tax to be scrapped. But economists who met the Finance Minister urged her to keep it and to keep the tax regime stable. Mr Agrawal's words: on the first of February, you will get to know.

For your corporate clients, a reminder that the tax board extended audit report and return deadlines for the 2026-27 assessment year by 21 days, and the extended audit report date falls this week, on the twenty-first.

One date for your calendar. New motor insurance rules start on the fifteenth of December. Policies will have four separate sections of cover, and some protection stays optional, so check whether your spouse, children or parents are actually covered as passengers.

On gold, the bullion association's rate on Monday put 24-carat gold at about 1,34,971 rupees per 10 grams, and silver at about 1,70,251 rupees a kilo. Prices are near one-year lows, but a strong dollar and rate-hike bets are still weighing on them.

A few quick ones. The pension regulator has relaxed address-proof rules for NRI seafarers opening NPS accounts. And consumer courts are on your side on small charges. A Jaipur restaurant was fined 10,000 rupees for rounding up a bill by 50 paise, and a Bengaluru store must pay 8,020 rupees for charging 20 rupees for a carry bag.

An investor warning: the FBI has traced a 400 million dollar crypto theft scheme called FaceStealer to North Korean hackers, and Livemint lists the steps to take if you were affected.

What to watch today: a flat start is likely, with the Nifty's 25,300 to 25,400 zone the hurdle. Nvidia's results land late tonight our time, so expect tech and IT names to react tomorrow. Crystal Crop's IPO opens tomorrow, and Anthropic lists on Thursday. That's your Market Brief. Have a good day.
